summary: Browser-submit harness: make the manual web-UI gate runnable (TKT-105 / TKT-190 follow-up)
description:
**As** a developer, **I want** the browser-submit check to be a command anyone can run, **so that** the one quality gate this repo cannot automate stops depending on whoever remembers to do it by hand.

### Why now

`AGENTS.md` has said *"There is no Playwright/e2e harness in-repo yet"* since **TKT-105**, and treats browser-submit as a permanently manual step. TKT-105 is also the ticket that proved the gap is not theoretical: Astro's CSRF guard 403'd **every** back-office write form, and TKT-102's forms had been silently broken the same way since they shipped — invisible to API smoke, which bypasses the SSR layer entirely.

**TKT-190 turned three browser-only behaviours into load-bearing security controls**, none of which any in-repo test can verify:
- that a browser sends `Origin` on a same-origin POST (the whole premise of the proxy-aware origin check that replaced `checkOrigin`);
- that a browser honours `SameSite=Lax` (one of the two CSRF controls);
- that a browser honours the cookie's `Path=/admin` scope (the fix for a review finding — the gateway serves four apps on one origin, so `Path=/` handed a live staff credential to all of them).

During TKT-190 a ~90-line Playwright script driving the already-installed system Chrome checked all three, plus the full sign-in / reload / sign-out / replay flow — **13/13**. It ran from a scratch directory and was deliberately not committed: a new dev dependency and a gate change is its own decision, not something to slip into an authentication ticket. This is that decision.

**Every remaining TKT-22 child is a UI ticket** (TKT-192 event builder, TKT-193 order console, TKT-197 role-aware nav), and TKT-194 adds refund actions. They will each carry the manual cost, and each will be verified by whatever the agent of the day improvises.

### In scope

- `playwright` as a dev dependency of the `web/` workspace, using the **system Chrome** (`channel: 'chrome'`) rather than downloading a bundled browser — the bundled build is what this repo's cached versions kept drifting from, and the browser people actually use is the better oracle.
- One `make browser-check` target that assumes a running `make up`.
- A first spec covering TKT-190's flow, ported from the script in that ticket's run.
- `AGENTS.md`: replace *"There is no Playwright/e2e harness in-repo yet"* with how to run it, and say plainly what it does and does not cover.

### Out of scope

- **Adding it to `make check` / CI.** That is the expensive half — it needs a running stack, a browser in CI, and an answer on flake tolerance. Decide it here explicitly and defer it to its own ticket if the answer is "not yet"; do not let it happen by accident.
- Porting the existing storefront or scanner flows. One spec, one ticket.
- Visual regression, accessibility audits, performance.

### Conditions of Success

- [ ] `make browser-check` runs against `make up` and exits non-zero when a check fails — proven by deliberately breaking one (e.g. flipping the cookie `Path` back to `/`) and observing the failure, not just by watching it pass.
- [ ] It covers, at minimum, TKT-190's three browser-only properties: a browser-composed same-origin form POST is accepted, the session cookie's stored attributes, and a genuine cross-site form POST from another origin minting no session.
- [ ] A staff account is provisioned by the harness or documented as a prerequisite; no credential is committed.
- [ ] It is **not** wired into `make check` unless this ticket explicitly decides to, and the decision is recorded either way.
- [ ] `AGENTS.md`'s quality-gates section names the command, and no longer claims no harness exists.
- [ ] `make check` still green, and no slower — the harness must not become an implicit dependency of the normal gate.

**Quality gates:** `make check` green; the change is dev-tooling only and touches no service code.

governingAdrs.why: The Astro SSR shell whose framework-level behaviour (checkOrigin, base-path rewrites, redirects) is exactly what API-level smoke cannot see — the reason this harness exists.
Records the three browser-dependent controls TKT-190 shipped: SameSite, the cookie Path scope, and the proxy-aware Origin check. This harness is what verifies them.

reference.summary: The incident that created the rule: an SSR CSRF guard 403'd every back-office write form, undetected for two tickets because API smoke bypasses the SSR layer.
AGENTS.md's quality-gates section — the 'no harness exists' claim this ticket retires.
The flow to port: gate, sign in, reload, sign out, replay, cross-site POST. TKT-190's smoke tests cover the HTTP half; this covers what only a browser decides.

objective.note: Named gap since TKT-105; TKT-190 made three browser-only behaviours load-bearing.

scope.note: In/out enumerated; the CI question is explicitly carved out as a decision to record, not to assume.

uncertainties.note: Should the harness eventually gate CI? Needs a browser in CI and a flake-tolerance answer. Not required to start — the ticket ships a runnable command either way.

dependencies.note: None; TKT-190 is merged and supplies the first spec's subject.

approach.note: Playwright against system Chrome, one make target, one spec.

first_slice.note: The TKT-190 flow, already written and proven 13/13 during that run.

success.note: COS require proving the harness FAILS when the thing it checks is broken.

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
Filed from **TKT-190**'s retro (owner approved 2026-08-03). The working script from that run is the
starting point — it drove real Google Chrome against `make up` and passed 13/13, including the
cookie-scope check that confirmed a review finding's fix from the browser's own behaviour rather
than from an assertion about it.

One `uncertainties` item is deliberately **open** with `owner: human`: whether this should ever gate
CI. The ticket is useful without answering it, and Gate 1 is hard-blocked while the item is open, so
the question gets asked rather than assumed.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
### Delivered by TKT-228 — recommend closing without separate work

Board validation on 2026-08-08 found this ticket still in Backlog while its substance had shipped
on 2026-08-06 as `a9b81de`, under the un-created key TKT-228.

Checked against this ticket's own asks, not merely by title:

| This ticket asked for | Shipped in `a9b81de` |
|---|---|
| browser-submit as "a command anyone can run" | `make browser` → `scripts/browser.sh` |
| specs committed, not per-ticket throwaways | `test/browser/reset-password.mjs`, now joined by `rate-limit.mjs` |
| the `AGENTS.md` "no Playwright/e2e harness in-repo yet" claim retired | rewritten to the `make browser` working agreement |
| the dev-dependency + gate decision taken deliberately | `package.json` / `pnpm-lock.yaml`, with a learning recording the failure mode |

**Not carried over:** this ticket's framing listed the three TKT-190 browser-only security
behaviours (`Origin` on same-origin POST, `SameSite=Lax`, cookie `Path=/admin` scoping) as the
motivating cases. The harness now exists, but the committed specs cover password reset and rate
limiting — **there is still no committed spec asserting those three staff-session behaviours.**
That is the only residue of this ticket, and it belongs to TKT-195 (back-office login) or a small
follow-up, not to re-opening the harness work.

Left in Backlog for the owner to close or re-scope to that residue — closing a ticket someone else
filed is a call for its filer.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### ❌ Delivered elsewhere — close without implementing

Backlog review 2026-08-25. This ticket's deliverable — "make the manual web-UI gate runnable" — shipped under **TKT-228**, which AGENTS.md records as promoting the browser specs "from per-ticket throwaway scripts".

At HEAD:
- `make browser` exists (`Makefile:172`, depends on `build-gate-linux build-ts`).
- `test/browser/` holds nine specs plus a `lib/`: `channels.mjs`, `event-builder.mjs`, `order-console.mjs`, `organizer-assertion.mjs`, `rate-limit.mjs`, `reset-password.mjs`, `slot-allocations.mjs`, `venue-authoring.mjs`.
- AGENTS.md carries the working agreement this ticket would have established, including the two hard-won rules that came out of using it: a browser spec cannot observe a request the SSR handler makes (TKT-244), and the R6 misrouting exercise that proved `make check` passes while all three browser specs fail.

The one item that was `open` here — **should the harness gate CI?** — is also answered, and answered NO: AGENTS.md states plainly that `make browser` "is not part of `make check` — it needs the host's real Chrome, so CI cannot run it." That is the decision this ticket was holding a human question for, recorded and in force.

No action. The DoR on this ticket is stale rather than unmet.
